summary: Creates the Student Experience Hub as the common digital starting point for students, combining a rapid first-release aggregation of essential information and services with the shared app and platform foundations for progressively deeper integrated journeys.
detailSummary:
The Student App and Journey Integration deliverable owns the Student Experience Hub as a student-facing product and shared technical platform. Its first production release will establish a useful daily starting point for students from September 2027, bringing together the information and routes they most frequently need rather than waiting for every underlying system or service to be transformed.

The first-year release will deliberately combine different depths of integration. King’s Edge will provide the deepest native product experience through the rapid replatforming and functionality delivered under 4.1.4. Alongside it, the Hub will surface priority information and actions from timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s through the safest practical combination of live feeds, widgets, authenticated hand-offs and dedicated Hub views. Students should be able to see what they need today, enter their learning spaces, discover and manage King’s Edge activity, ask a question and see open Ask King’s enquiries from one coherent home.

This requires a rapid integration shakeout before substantial build decisions are fixed. For each priority source, the team will establish what can be integrated safely, what remains authoritative elsewhere, what is likely to be replatformed later and where temporary or disposable integration work is justified by immediate student value. Those decisions will be explicit and the integrations will be isolated so that changing an underlying source does not require the student experience to be rebuilt.

The wider Hub will then deepen iteratively. Prototypes and working alphas will be tested with students during 2026/27, the combined service will be feature-complete and hardened by the end of July 2027, and August will be reserved for launch readiness ahead of the September release. Broader systems mapping, journey research and service design will continue alongside delivery so that later phases can move from aggregation and intelligent hand-off towards genuinely integrated end-to-end student journeys.

caseForChange.problem:
Students currently encounter King’s through a fragmented collection of portals, applications, websites and organisational routes. Information and functionality are structured around the systems and teams that provide them rather than around what a student is trying to do. Even common daily needs such as seeing a timetable, entering learning spaces, finding opportunities or asking for support require students to know which destination to use.

King’s therefore lacks a single useful place from which a student can begin their digital day. This fragmentation weakens the value of services and information that already exist, creates avoidable cognitive effort and particularly disadvantages students who are less familiar with institutional structures or less able to rely on informal knowledge.

The underlying digital estate will not become simple quickly. Core systems, data foundations and service platforms will continue to change over several years. Waiting for that transformation before creating a coherent student-facing experience would defer visible benefit, while building only a deep King’s Edge product would miss the opportunity to establish the shared front door from the outset.
caseForChange.opportunity:
The Student Experience Hub can provide an immediately useful horizontal layer across the existing estate while deeper transformation continues underneath it.

The first release can focus on the small number of sources that matter most to students’ everyday navigation: King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s. Where safe feeds and interfaces exist, the Hub can surface information directly. Where deeper integration is not yet proportionate, it can provide a coherent widget, authenticated hand-off or dedicated Hub view into the authoritative service. This creates a genuine daily front door without pretending every source system has already been replaced.

King’s Edge can simultaneously remain the deepest native product domain, using the common platform to deliver richer discovery, participation, projects, planning, evidence and recognition. A deliberately replaceable integration layer allows the wider Hub to aggregate useful information now, accept bounded temporary work where justified, and substitute new institutional platforms later without rebuilding the student experience.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge is already moving into rapid replatforming and substantial product development, creating the shared application foundations and delivery momentum from which the wider Hub can grow. At the same time, students continue to experience the practical cost of fragmented digital entry points, while timetabling, KEATS, CRM and wider student-systems work create integration decisions that cannot sensibly be postponed.

The first academic year is therefore a valuable mobilisation window. A rapid integration shakeout can identify which priority feeds are safe and useful now, where known future replatforming should shape the design, and which temporary integrations are worth accepting for early student value.

Working iteratively through prototypes, alphas and beta releases during 2026/27 creates enough evidence to reach a hardened release candidate by the end of July 2027, reserve August for operational readiness and launch the Student Experience Hub as the normal digital starting point for students in September 2027.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
From September 2027, students have one coherent digital place from which to begin their day at King’s.

The Student Experience Hub provides a shared home and navigation layer that surfaces the day’s timetable, useful KEATS learning entry points, King’s Edge activity and discovery, and Ask King’s enquiry entry and open-case information. The depth of integration varies deliberately by source, with authoritative systems retained where appropriate and students handed off coherently when a task still needs to be completed elsewhere.

King’s Edge continues to develop as the first deep native product domain, while the common Hub shell, identity, profile, navigation, telemetry and integration patterns are designed for reuse. Broader student journeys can then be integrated progressively as service, data and system readiness improves.

Over time, the Hub moves from aggregation and intelligent hand-off towards a more personalised and integrated institutional relationship with students, while temporary integrations can be replaced cleanly and duplicated entry points rationalised when continuity is assured.

benefits.title: Students have one useful place to start their day
benefits.statement: A common student home brings together the most important daily information and routes across timetable, learning, support and King’s Edge, reducing the need to remember and navigate separate institutional destinations.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the September 2027 first release, strengthening as integrations deepen
benefits.successLooksLike: Students routinely use the Hub as their starting point and can reach common daily information and actions with fewer destinations, fewer dead ends and less dependence on institutional knowledge.

benefits.title: Access to provision becomes more equitable
benefits.statement: A consistent digital starting point and clearer discovery routes make services, learning information and opportunities more visible to students who are less able to rely on informal knowledge, confidence or existing networks.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, particularly those currently less well served by fragmented provision
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first release, increasing with personalisation and deeper integration
benefits.successLooksLike: Relevant provision reaches a broader range of students and differences in discovery, navigation or take-up between student groups begin to narrow.

benefits.title: King’s creates a reusable and replaceable student-app platform
benefits.statement: Shared product, platform and integration patterns allow King’s to create immediate student value from existing sources while isolating temporary integrations and reducing repeated development as underlying systems change.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, product teams and King’s
benefits.owner: TBC – Student Experience Hub product and platform owner
benefits.realisationPeriod: Increasing from the first live integrations and as common capabilities are reused
benefits.successLooksLike: New requirements reuse the Hub’s common foundations where appropriate, temporary integrations can be replaced without rebuilding the student experience, and redundant portals or repeated functions can be retired safely over time.

steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the product, architecture and technical foundations for the Student Experience Hub, supporting both the rapid King’s Edge replatform and a broader student home that can aggregate priority sources safely.

steps.title: Triage the priority integrations and lock the first-release scope
steps.summary: From September to December 2026, rapidly assess King’s Edge, timetabling, KEATS and Ask King’s to determine what can be surfaced safely for September 2027, the appropriate depth of integration, likely replatforming risk and where deliberately temporary work is justified.

steps.title: Prototype the common student home and target experience
steps.summary: From November 2026 to April 2027, put increasingly realistic versions of the common student home in front of students, testing how timetable, KEATS, Ask King’s and King’s Edge should appear together while continuing focused journey research and service design.

steps.title: Build the reusable Hub kernel and priority aggregations alongside King’s Edge
steps.summary: From January to June 2027, build the shared shell, identity, navigation, profile, telemetry and replaceable integration layer while the deep King’s Edge product develops under 4.1.4. Connect the priority timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s information and hand-offs into the same student home.

steps.title: Put a working alpha with live priority feeds into student hands
steps.summary: From February to April 2027, move beyond clickable prototypes into a working alpha for a bounded student cohort, using real priority integrations where safe and measuring whether the Hub works as a useful daily starting point.

steps.title: Run a broader beta of the daily student home
steps.summary: From April to June 2027, expand testing of the combined home, refine information hierarchy and widget behaviour, improve accessibility and responsive performance, and resolve the most important integration and support weaknesses.

steps.title: Harden the September release candidate
steps.summary: From May through July 2027, freeze the first-release scope and complete security, privacy, accessibility, performance, resilience, recovery, monitoring and operational-readiness work. The product should be feature-complete by the end of July, with August reserved for final regression, launch rehearsal and controlled fixes.

steps.title: Launch the Student Experience Hub as the daily digital front door
steps.summary: Launch in September 2027 with a shared student home that brings together King’s Edge, timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s at deliberately different depths of integration, establishing the Hub as the normal place students begin their digital day.

steps.title: Operate, learn and deepen the first shared front door
steps.summary: From September 2027 to February 2028, use live evidence to improve reliability, navigation and usefulness, deepen priority integrations where justified, and identify the service and journey changes that should move next from aggregation into genuinely integrated experience.

steps.title: Approve the deeper app roadmap and first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, combine live Hub evidence, systems and information-flow evidence, student-journey research and learning from King’s Edge to select the first non-Edge areas that should move beyond aggregation and hand-off into deeper integrated journeys.

steps.title: Deepen the shared app with the first end-to-end non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Build the first selected deeper journeys into the existing student home, connecting authoritative data and CRM-enabled interactions where ready while retaining source systems where they continue to add specialist value.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common app capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration, progressively replacing shallow hand-offs where deeper integration adds clear value.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: Shift the centre of product demand towards the broader student experience, integrate additional systems and service journeys, and use common Hub capabilities to help students navigate information, opportunities, actions, progress and support through a more coherent institutional relationship.

steps.title: Consolidate the Hub and rationalise parallel entry points
steps.summary: Establish the Student Experience Hub as the primary student-facing product and platform, with enduring product ownership, platform governance, service management, cost ownership and product analytics. Progressively retire or rationalise duplicated portals and repeated functionality where continuity is assured, while retaining specialist source systems and interfaces where they continue to add necessary value.
